name: Rethinking Memory in AI: Taxonomy, Operations, Topics, and Future Directions (a.k.a. v3 title: Rethinking Memory in LLM based Agents: Representations, Operations, and Emerging Topics) (Du et al.)
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2505.00675, cs.CL); submitted 1 May 2025, last revised 24 Dec 2025 (v3). No peer-reviewed venue identified as of mid-2026.
authors_affiliation: Yiming Du, Wenyu Huang, Danna Zheng, Zhaowei Wang, Sebastien Montella, Mirella Lapata, Kam-Fai Wong, Jeff Z. Pan. Affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong; The University of Edinburgh; HKUST; Poisson Lab, CSI, Huawei UK R&D Ltd. (work done during Yiming Du's visit to University of Edinburgh).
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/Elvin-Yiming-Du/Survey_Memory_in_AI (the 'Memory Compass' continuously-updated paper/dataset/tools list; ~350 stars, last push Dec 2025, MIT license, includes a 'Week Papers' rolling update section)
task_domain: Survey/taxonomy of memory in LLM-based agents, spanning QA, long-term conversational/personalized dialogue, long-context modeling, knowledge editing (parametric modification), and multi-source/multi-agent memory; not a single task method.
problem_setting: A survey that reframes memory in AI/LLM-based agents through atomic operations and representation types. Setting is conceptual/organizational rather than experimental: it argues prior surveys emphasize application-level memory use (e.g., personalized dialogue) while overlooking the atomic operations governing memory dynamics. It covers both offline (parametric/pretrained memory, knowledge editing) and interactive/online (episodic, multi-session, agentic) settings, and both single-agent and multi-agent/multi-source memory. Supervision availability varies by surveyed sub-topic; the survey itself provides taxonomy, dataset tables, and a tools landscape rather than new supervised training.
what_is_retrieved: Across surveyed systems: external contextual memory items including documents, dialogue/episodic histories, personas, knowledge-graph nodes/relations, multimodal content (text/image/audio/video), and structured KB entries; Retrieval is one of the six defined atomic operations. Parametric memory is 'accessed' via feedforward computation rather than explicit retrieval.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID at the survey level: the taxonomy explicitly spans STATIC external corpora/KBs/documents, GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes (long-term, multi-session), and parametric (in-weights) memory, plus multi-source memory that fuses several stores.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Not a single objective; the survey describes Retrieval generically and reports retrieval metrics such as Recall@K and NDCG@K (e.g., for LongMemEval) used by surveyed benchmarks, i.e., top-k ranking objectives, alongside end-to-end accuracy. No unified completeness-vs-topk stance is taken. [uncertain]
retrieval_unit: Heterogeneous across the survey: documents/passages, dialogue turns and multi-session histories, episodic experiences/trajectories, knowledge-graph subgraphs/triples, persona facts, and multimodal segments. Retrieval is defined formally as selecting relevant memory entries from the contextual memory store conditioned on a query.
index_source: Both: static corpora and offline-induced parametric memory, plus online/test-time-induced growing memory (Consolidation writes short-term experiences into persistent memory; Indexing organizes the contextual store). Hybrid construction is explicitly covered (multi-source memory).
index_structure_topology: Surveyed across topologies: flat vector indices (FAISS, Chroma, Milvus, Qdrant, Weaviate), knowledge/temporal GRAPH stores (Neo4j, Graphiti, knowledge-graph memory), and hierarchical/structured organizations. Indexing is defined as a distinct operation that builds structures (e.g., indices, graphs) over stored memory for efficient access.
retriever_type: Surveys the full spectrum: sparse BM25, dense retrievers (Contriever, embedding models), graph-based retrieval, and LLM-driven retrieval; hybrid retrieval is discussed. No single retriever is proposed.
retriever_learning_signal: Not a contribution of the survey; surveyed retrievers range from off-the-shelf (BM25, OpenAI embeddings) to contrastively-trained dense retrievers (Contriever) to LM-feedback / task-effectiveness-driven memory retrieval discussed within long-term and multi-source memory topics. No unified learning signal is prescribed. [uncertain]
query_construction: Varies by surveyed system: raw user query, dialogue-context-conditioned query, decomposed sub-queries for multi-hop QA, and temporally-conditioned queries; the survey formalizes Retrieval as conditioned on a query but does not prescribe a single construction method.
query_granularity: Both task-level and step/turn-level retrieval are covered (e.g., per-turn retrieval in long-term dialogue vs. one-shot retrieval in QA). No single granularity. [uncertain]
when_to_retrieve: Covers one-shot and iterative/interactive retrieval as used by surveyed long-term and agentic-memory systems; the survey does not advocate a single retrieval-timing policy. [uncertain]
retrieval_trigger_signal: Not standardized by the survey; surveyed systems use fixed schedules, agent-initiated requests, and reflection/condensation triggers. The six-operation framework treats Retrieval as triggered during utilization but does not catalog a single trigger signal. [uncertain]
reranking: Reranking is mentioned within retrieval pipelines of surveyed systems (e.g., retrieve-then-rerank), and benchmarks report NDCG@K implying ranking quality, but the survey does not propose a reranking method. [uncertain]
retrieved_context_refinement: Compression/Condensation is one of the six defined operations: it summarizes/distills retrieved or stored memory before use (reducing redundancy while preserving salient information). The survey thus frames post-retrieval refinement primarily as compression/condensation, alongside indexing-based filtering.
tool_document_engineering: N/A — the survey covers memory tools/frameworks (FAISS, LangChain, EasyEdit, Mem0, MemOS, etc.) rather than tool-retrieval document engineering; BFCL V4 is listed for CRUD tool-usage memory but tool-description engineering is not a focus. [uncertain]
index_content_separation: Implicitly covered via the Indexing operation (lightweight index structures over a larger memory store) and component-level vector/graph databases, but the survey does not frame a dedicated progressive-disclosure / index-then-content pattern as a contribution. [uncertain]
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Partly relevant: the tools landscape includes dynamic/temporally-aware stores (Graphiti) and CRUD tool-usage memory (BFCL V4 'Memory' category); MCP/RapidAPI protocols are not a survey focus. [uncertain]
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A — inter-tool dependency modeling is not within the survey's memory-operations scope.
how_retrieved_used: Across surveyed systems: prompt/context augmentation (memory-grounded generation), parametric injection via knowledge editing/fine-tuning (parametric modification topic), and graph/structured grounding. The survey's Utilization category covers Retrieval + Compression feeding generation.
planning_integration: Not the survey's focus; memory is positioned as supporting coherent long-term agent interaction. Retrieve-then-generate and per-turn memory access are described for agentic settings, but planning integration (MCTS/tree-search) is not a primary axis. [uncertain]
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Varies across surveyed systems (per-answer for QA, per-turn/per-session for long-term dialogue); the survey does not standardize interleaving granularity. [uncertain]
retrieved_item_representation: Surface forms surveyed include raw text/dialogue, distilled summaries (via Compression/Condensation), structured knowledge-graph notes, and parametric (latent, in-weights) representations. The survey's representation taxonomy is parametric vs contextual (unstructured/structured).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Spans raw episodic experiences/trajectories, distilled/condensed summaries, structured guidelines/KB entries, and parametric knowledge; the survey's organizing abstraction is the parametric-vs-contextual representation split rather than a single abstraction level.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Discussed via memory hallucination/omission and forgetting: e.g., HaluMem evaluates hallucination/omission in memory extraction/updating/retrieval, and Forgetting is a defined operation for pruning outdated/irrelevant memory. No single robustness mechanism is proposed by the survey. [uncertain]
memory_type: All types in scope: parametric (in-weights), episodic/long-term, graph (knowledge-graph/temporal), workflow/procedural, and latent — the survey explicitly unifies these under parametric vs contextual (unstructured/structured) representations.
write_back: Yes (as a surveyed capability): Consolidation writes short-term experiences into persistent memory and Updating modifies stored entries; these are two of the six defined operations. The survey itself does not implement write-back but catalogs it.
online_growth: Yes (covered): long-term and multi-source memory systems grow the store during deployment via Consolidation/Updating; parametric memory grows via parametric modification (knowledge editing). The survey treats online memory growth as central.
write_back_trigger: Not standardized by the survey; surveyed triggers include per-interaction consolidation, reflective/condensation-driven writes, and explicit knowledge-edit operations. The framework defines Consolidation and Updating as the write operations but does not prescribe a single trigger. [uncertain]
failure_experience_usage: Not a dedicated axis; the survey emphasizes Forgetting (pruning outdated/incorrect memory) and memory updating/correction (e.g., HaluMem hallucination/omission, MemoryBench retention) rather than explicit success-vs-failure contrastive storage. [uncertain]
memory_evolution_update: Explicitly covered: Updating (delta/refine-overwrite of existing entries) and Forgetting (prune) are defined operations; Consolidation appends/encodes new entries; the survey describes memory as temporally evolving (link-and-evolve via temporal knowledge graphs such as Graphiti).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Not a survey-wide claim; surveyed systems mostly use similarity-based or rule-based retrieval, with learned/RL retrieval discussed only for specific surveyed works. The survey does not frame retrieval-as-learned-policy as a central axis. [uncertain]
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Yes — Multi-source Memory is one of the four key topics, covering integration/sharing of memory across sources and (in part) across agents/frameworks; this is explicitly highlighted as an emerging direction.
benchmarks: Survey catalogs benchmark/dataset tables rather than running them. Long-term memory: PersonaMem-v2, MemoryBench, HaluMem, BFCL V4, LongMemEval, LoCoMo, MemoryBank, PerLTQA, MaLP/MALP, DialSim, MovieChat-1K, Conversation-Chronicles (CC), LaMP, MSC, DuLeMon, 2WikiMultiHopQA, NQ, HotpotQA. Long-context: MMLongBench, WikiText-103, PG-19, LRA, and others. Plus parametric-memory-modification (knowledge editing) and multi-source memory evaluation tables.
benchmark_family: memory (LoCoMo, LongMemEval, PersonaMem, MemoryBench, HaluMem, MemoryBank, PerLTQA, MSC, DuLeMon); QA / multi-hop (NQ, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA); long-context (PG-19, WikiText-103, LRA, MMLongBench); tool/function-calling (BFCL V4); multimodal/long-video (MovieChat-1K); personalization (LaMP, MaLP).
baselines: N/A — as a survey it does not run head-to-head baseline comparisons; it organizes prior methods (e.g., MemoryBank, knowledge-editing methods, RAG systems, long-context models) within the operation/topic taxonomy.
key_metrics: Reports the metrics used by catalogued benchmarks: Accuracy, Recall@K, NDCG@K, EM, F1, ROUGE, BLEU, MAP, Precision/Recall, PPL, GPT-4 score, Persona Score, Hallucination/Omission Rate, Retention Rate, AST Accuracy / Execution Success (BFCL). No single headline metric is computed by the survey.
headline_result: N/A — no experimental headline number; the survey's contribution is the taxonomy of two memory representations (parametric vs contextual) and six atomic operations (Consolidation, Updating, Indexing, Forgetting, Retrieval, Compression/Condensation) mapped to four topics (long-term, long-context, parametric modification, multi-source). Most-cited framing number: 6 operations x 2 representations -> 4 topics.
ablations: N/A — no empirical ablations are run; the survey instead maps which operations each topic and each benchmark exercises (e.g., dataset tables tag the operations evaluated, such as 'Indexing, Retrieval, Compression' for LongMemEval/LoCoMo).
evaluation_decoupling: Reports, via catalogued benchmarks, that intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@K, NDCG@K, MAP) and end-to-end task metrics (Accuracy, F1, ROUGE) are sometimes reported separately (e.g., LongMemEval, PerLTQA), but the survey does not enforce decoupling itself.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mixed across catalogued benchmarks: most score final outcomes (Accuracy/F1), while some add process-oriented signals (Retention Rate for continual learning, Hallucination/Omission Rate for memory faithfulness, temporal-reasoning subsets). The survey itself reports no process metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Not quantified by the survey; efficiency is discussed qualitatively for long-context memory (compression to reduce KV/context cost) and Indexing for efficient access, but no retrieval-call counts, latency, or cost numbers are produced by the survey. [uncertain]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Not prescribed; long-context and Compression/Condensation discussions address budget pressure (context window, KV cache, summary length), but the survey sets no fixed-k or budget-cap policy of its own. [uncertain]
survey_scope_and_axes: Two organizing axes: (1) Memory representation — Parametric vs Contextual (Contextual split into Unstructured and Structured); (2) Six atomic memory operations grouped into Memory Management (Consolidation, Indexing, Updating, Forgetting) and Memory Utilization (Retrieval, Compression; renamed Condensation in v3). These map to four key research topics: long-term memory, long-context memory, parametric memory modification, and multi-source memory. The survey also catalogs benchmark datasets and a four-level tools landscape (Components / Framework / Application-Layer / Product) and a Human-vs-AI memory comparison plus future directions. Reference coverage: ~310 bibliography entries (v2); coverage window through 2025 (continuously updated repo through Dec 2025).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A — the survey does not construct a benchmark; it aggregates existing datasets in comparison tables annotated with modality, supported operations, dataset type (QA vs multi-session), persona presence, temporal-reasoning presence, metrics, purpose, and year.
builds_on: Prior memory surveys it extends/critiques, e.g., Zhang et al. 2024 (operational view: writing/management/reading, but missing indexing), long-context surveys (Huang et al. 2023b), long-term memory surveys (He et al. 2024d; Jiang et al. 2024b), personalization (Liu et al. 2025a), and knowledge-editing surveys (Wang et al. 2024h). Grounds memory operations in cognitive-science notions (e.g., Consolidation: Squire et al. 2015).
contrasts_with: Application-centric memory surveys that emphasize use cases (e.g., personalized conversational memory) without a unified operational framework; and subtopic-narrow surveys (long-context-only, long-term-only, editing-only). Du et al. argue these miss atomic operations such as Indexing and lack cohesive architectural/operational views plus practical benchmark/tool foundations.
lineage: Surveys group. A foundational taxonomy/operations survey for memory in LLM-based agents; provides the parametric-vs-contextual representation split and six-operation lifecycle that situates RAG (Retrieval), memory consolidation/updating, and knowledge editing (parametric modification) within one framework — a reference map for memory-augmented and retrieval-augmented agent lines of work.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A — not a case-based reasoning work; the survey does not frame itself around CBR Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain phases (though its Retrieval/Updating/Consolidation/Forgetting operations partially parallel CBR mechanisms).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False — the survey does not explicitly frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; its operations are grounded in cognitive memory science and LLM-agent literature instead.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A — no CBR case-adaptation mechanism; the closest surveyed mechanisms are Updating (refine stored memory) and Compression/Condensation (distill memory), described across surveyed systems rather than as a single adaptation method.
